attacked.target: The receipt of 5,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH, and is recognized on the date of receipt, 2026-06-28.
attacked.evidence:
Section 115BBH of the Income-tax Act, 2025, defines “transfer” in relation to virtual digital assets.
**(3)** For the purposes of this section, the word "transfer" as defined in clause (47) of section 2, shall apply to any virtual digital asset, whether capital asset or not.
.
attacked.attack: Under section 115BBH, the term 'transfer' is specifically defined in relation to virtual digital assets. However, the reasoning provided does not address whether the mere receipt of USDC qualifies as a 'transfer' under this definition. Without establishing that a transfer occurred, s.115BBH cannot be directly applied.

attacked.target: No provision in the text prescribes a specific method for determining the rupee value of USDC on the valuation date.
attacked.attack: Rule 206 specifies the rate of exchange for calculating the value in rupees of income expressed in foreign currency. Since the income in question involves USDC, a virtual digital asset excluded from foreign currency under clause (n) of unamended section 2 of the FEMA Act, application of the cited provision to reckon valuation dates with respect to s.92 becomes incorrect. An exception for cryptocurrencies lacks requisite amendment in this statute.
attacked.evidence: Clause (m) "foreign currency" means any currency other than Indian currency; Clause (47A) "virtual digital asset" means… (a) any information or code or number or token (not being Indian currency or foreign currency), (night be present), sub-rule §(4)  inserted w.e.f. 1-4-2026 ***PROVIDED THAT*** the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, exclude any digital asset from the definition of virtual digital asset.

checked_and_survived: The supply does not meet all conditions for being an export of services.
limits: The precise definitions and applicability of 'transfer' in the context of virtual digital assets need further clarification from legal experts or additional statutory guidance.
